summary: The battle screen renders its presentation registries instead of reading them for labels: a vfx_factory builds a real particle-and-shader effect per presentation.vfx record, camera beats and hit-stop come from presentation.camera, the band rail eases, damage numbers carry weight, the ward line is a drawn shimmering line, grave watch pulses on hostiles, death dissolves, and the paper rigs get a lighting pass that sits them in the plate.

coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at f5d26d1. BASELINE, read before any code was written (docs/verification/captures has no `before` file because the card asks for six beats of the finished screen; the fault list is here): the paper rigs floated roughly a hundred pixels above the painted terrace with no contact shadow, no rim light and no plate colour on them, so they read as stickers on a photograph; there was no effect of any kind on screen, the vfx registry being consumed only as tooltip prose; no camera, no hit-stop, no shake; no damage numbers; the band rail was a flat corner list whose names clipped (MICHAEL CORRIGA) and whose Composure pips ran off the card edge; Michael's command grid was folded into a portrait card too small to read a word in; the skill diamonds sat loose on the stone with grey-on-grey labels; the enemy intent line vanished into the bright sky; and the paper stage's teal and red layout guide arcs were drawn in the running game. THE RECORD IS THE OWNER: vfx_factory.gd builds every effect from its record and nothing else, and paper_doll.gd's `draw_presentation_vfx` -- which hand-drew three specific vfx ids -- had to be deleted for that to be true (move 2, replace); its `draw_betty` (no caller) and `draw_raptor` (unreachable behind razorbeak_rig == null) went with it (move 3). REGISTRY FIELDS ADDED, with validator lines: `socket` (a closed set of fourteen live rig sockets), `emitter` (none/burst/ring/crescent/beam/trail/motes/panel) and `direction` (none/outward/inward/upward/downward/forward/backward/along_line) on all 46 vfx entries; `anchor` and `motion` stay the authored art words a painter reads, and several anchors map to one socket (an ampoule and a mace core are both carried in the main hand), which is a mapping, not two answers to one question. The validator also holds every authored palette word to a colour BattlePalette.EFFECT_COLORS can resolve, and battle_presentation_test.gd asserts the same pair, so a word added to one without the other fails rather than rendering black. PALETTE: lane/P5-grammar-and-surface had pushed nothing when this lane finished, so game/themes/bronze_vellum.tres does not exist; battle_palette.gd gathers the prototype's own DEEP/PANEL/CREAM/TEAL/BRONZE/DANGER/MUTED at their existing values plus the effect vocabulary, with a comment naming the Theme as the owner that replaces them. AYLA'S COLOURS ARE OPEN: her nine records carry the literal `palette_unestablished_pending_ayla_identity_lock`, and the factory renders them in one neutral constant marked `needs decision` rather than choosing for her. GRAVE WATCH WITHOUT A NEW SNAPSHOT KEY: the snapshot carries no site rules and Rust is not this lane's, so the screen reads the `site_rule.round.<n>` command id the bridge already writes on the Guard a rule hands out at the round boundary -- nothing else writes it -- and pulses the hostiles that received it. RENDERING FACTS FOUND BY CAPTURE, not assumed: a CanvasGroup composite with an edge-detecting rim shader renders nothing on this project's declared gl_compatibility path (a flat magenta shader on the group came back as an unchanged figure), so the lighting pass is a drawn backlight texture, per-piece shade modulation and a parent-material shader for the bleed and the dissolve; and a ShaderMaterial and two `_draw` implementations on the contact-shadow node all came back invisible while the effect layer's ring, beam, crescent and panel shaders rendered in the same frame, so the contact shadow is a radial GradientTexture2D. Both are noted in the code beside the choice. TWO CAPTURE BEATS ARE DRIVEN AND SAY SO: software rendering here runs at a few frames a second, too slow to catch a 190 ms effect inside the real playback clock, so the impact beat's authored cue is handed to the screen directly with the engine clock slowed; and no code path in battle.rs calls `spend_composure` outside its own tests, so no fight in this tree can produce a Shaken actor and that beat is driven by a snapshot carrying the status in the bridge's exact shape. BLOCKED, NOT FAKED: Ayla's seven commands cannot be SUBMITTED through the debug battle -- the fixture starts her at bond rank D (battle.rs `prototype_vertical_slice`) and no authored scene in this tree raises her, so A10's gate refuses her rank A ward line and above. All sixteen records are still PLAYED through the same director path a submitted command uses, which is what the card's assertion is about; a suite that submits her kit needs either a campaign whose scenes raise Ayla or a fixture change, and both belong to A-lane cards. The card says fourteen skills (Betty's seven and Ayla's seven); Michael's two play on the same screen through the same director and are exercised too, so the suite covers sixteen.
